The Devīmāhātmya is the best-known Sanskrit text on the Goddess and is still recited during Navarātri. The lecture reads key passages in translation and sets them beside sculpture and painting to show how the Śākta tradition took shape.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • Where the text sits in the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa
  • Its three episodes: Madhu and Kaiṭabha, Mahiṣāsura, Śumbha and Niśumbha
  • Key passages read in translation
  • The Goddess in sculpture and painting

How the time is spent

  1. Text and history 20 min

    Context of Devīmāhātmya within Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.

    You: text timeline

  2. Image interpretation 45 min

    Compare selected goddess iconographies.

    You: visual notebook

  3. Interpretive dialogue 25 min

    Keep doctrinal, literary and material readings distinct.

    You: reflective essay

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Explain where the Devīmāhātmya sits within the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa and its historical context.
  • Outline its three episodes: Madhu and Kaiṭabha, Mahiṣāsura, and Śumbha and Niśumbha.
  • Compare the Goddess in sculpture and painting, keeping doctrinal, literary and material readings distinct.
